attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The formal cone argument is complete, but the substantive gap is proving that the actual RG compactness topology controls reflected product observables, especially near the reflection plane and for nonlocal Wilson-loop probes. Without that domination estimate, the closed cone may be valid in tau_OS but irrelevant to the constructed continuum limit.
steps: Fix a positive-time gauge-invariant algebra A_+^{gi}, including smeared local composites and Wilson-loop cylinder observables, and require all cutoff embeddings iota_{a,L} to preserve reflection and products on separated supports.
For each finite tuple f=(f_1,...,f_n) and coefficient vector c, define q_{f,c}(S)=sum_{i,j} conjugate(c_i)c_j S((theta f_i)f_j).
Equip the space of candidate Schwinger functionals with tau_OS, the initial topology generated by the maps q_{f,c}.

Because [0,infty) is closed in R and q_{f,c} is continuous by construction, the set q_{f,c}^{-1}([0,infty)) is closed; intersecting over all finite tuples gives a closed convex cone of OS-positive functionals.
Reflection positivity at each cutoff gives q_{iota f,c}(S_{a,L}) >= 0 for all finite probes supported in positive time.
If the RG limit satisfies q_{iota_{a_k,L_k} f,c}(S_{a_k,L_k}) -> q_{f,c}(S), then q_{f,c}(S) >= 0 for every finite tuple, giving OS positivity of S.
The derivation becomes a full Yang-Mills bridge only if tau_RG convergence implies this tau_OS convergence and the observable algebra is demonstrably unchanged across cutoff removal.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It proves conditional preservation of positivity, not existence of a Yang-Mills continuum theory satisfying all OS axioms. The missing analytic estimate must show that the RG construction converges on exactly the reflected quadratic forms, and the same-theory condition must rule out a positivity statement on a smaller or altered gauge-invariant algebra.

assumptions: For every cutoff pair (a,L), the regulated lattice or finite-volume theory satisfies reflection positivity on gauge-invariant observables supported in positive Euclidean time.
The reflection theta and the discretization maps commute on the chosen probe algebra up to errors that vanish in tau_OS.
The RG compactness/convergence topology controls S_{a,L}((theta f_i)f_j) for every finite reflected product appearing in OS positivity.
Reflection-plane contact terms are either absent for the chosen positive-time algebra or are renormalized by counterterms compatible with reflection positivity.
The limiting functional S is defined on the same algebra A_+^{gi}, not on a smaller quotient that would make the positivity statement valid but physically weaker.
definitions: source object: a net S_{a,L} of cutoff gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals on a fixed positive-time observable algebra A_+^{gi}, with reflection theta and discretization maps iota_{a,L} that are product-compatible on separated supports.

target object: a continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional S whose finite reflected quadratic forms are nonnegative, so that the OS reconstruction pre-Hilbert inner product is positive semidefinite.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, controlled only through convergence of finite reflected quadratic forms rather than through a transfer-matrix argument after the limit.

same-theory condition: the cutoff observables iota_{a,L}(f) and the continuum observable f represent the same gauge-invariant sector, with no change of algebra from gauge fixing, quotienting, or dropping Wilson-loop/local-composite probes during cutoff removal.
tau_OS is the weakest topology making every map S -> q_{f,c}(S) continuous for finite f_i in A_+^{gi} and coefficients c_i in C.
The reflection-positive cone C_OS is the intersection over all finite probes of q_{f,c}^{-1}([0,infty)), hence is formally closed once tau_OS is valid for the RG limit.

equations.valid_when: Valid for finite f_i in the fixed positive-time gauge-invariant algebra and coefficients c_i in C, with products interpreted in the common cutoff/continuum observable algebra.

equations.label: closed cone identity
equations.valid_when: Valid by definition of tau_OS as the initial topology for all finite reflected quadratic forms.

equations.label: cutoff transfer
equations.valid_when: Valid only if RG convergence dominates tau_OS for the reflected products (theta f_i)f_j and the discretization maps preserve the same-theory observable labels.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier would be a finite positive-time gauge-invariant tuple f_i and coefficients c_i for which S_{a,L} converges in the advertised RG topology but q_{f,c}(S) is either undefined or negative; that would show the topology is not valid for OS transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the purely topological part of the RG-to-OS passage: positivity preservation is automatic after the right convergence topology and fixed gauge-invariant algebra are secured.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let A_+^{gi} be a fixed gauge-invariant positive-time test algebra with reflection theta, and let tau_OS be the initial locally convex topology on Schwinger functionals generated by all finite OS quadratic forms q_{f,c}(S)=sum_{i,j} conjugate(c_i)c_j S((theta f_i)f_j). Then the reflection-positive functionals form a closed convex cone in tau_OS. Consequently, any regulated reflection-positive net S_{a,L} that converges to S in tau_OS has an OS-positive continuum limit on A_+^{gi}.

assumptions: Balaban-style polymer or block-spin bounds control gauge-invariant composite insertions across opposite time half-spaces.
The counterterm scheme is local and reflection symmetric, so reflected products are not assigned asymmetric finite parts.
There is a continuity theorem in the time-support parameter allowing plane-safe positivity to pass to the closed positive-time half-space.
definitions: A reflected product probe is the composite observable obtained by multiplying a negative-time reflected copy theta f_i with a positive-time observable f_j before taking the Schwinger functional.
Plane-safe probes have positive-time supports at distance at least epsilon from t=0; the full A_+^{gi} positivity claim is obtained only after an epsilon down to 0 extension estimate.
Dominance means that every seminorm needed for tau_OS is bounded by, or is a limit of, seminorms already controlled by the RG compactness topology.

equations.label: topology domination
equations.valid_when: Valid only after every reflected product seminorm defining tau_OS is shown to be continuous with respect to tau_RG.

equations.label: plane extension
equations.valid_when: Valid when time translations or mollified support shifts f^{(epsilon)} -> f are continuous in the reconstructed Schwinger topology and introduce no negative contact contribution.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a reflected Wilson-loop product has a divergent or scheme-dependent contact term at the reflection plane, the domination claim fails even though ordinary local Schwinger distributions may converge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the analytic bridge obligation hidden behind the formal closed-cone lemma.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the multiscale RG estimates give convergence of every renormalized reflected product (theta f_i)f_j, uniformly over finite probe families with support bounded away from the reflection plane before the final continuity extension, then RG convergence implies tau_OS convergence.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if one can exhibit a reflected finite quadratic form whose value is not determined by the multiscale convergence topology, or if reflection-plane contact terms cannot be made reflection-symmetric and nonnegative.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named RG seminorm family is proven to control S((theta f_i)f_j) for all finite gauge-invariant positive-time probes, with a valid extension from plane-safe supports to the full OS algebra.
control_decision.reason: Keep the branch, but stop treating closedness itself as the hard lemma. The next useful work is to attack or falsify the RG-dominates-OS-probes obligation.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal closed-cone theorem and a separate analytic domination theorem tau_RG => tau_OS for reflected products.
Must be fixed before the limit and must include enough local-composite and Wilson-loop probes to preserve the same theory; positivity on a reduced algebra is not sufficient.
The needed topology is not generic distributional convergence but convergence of every finite OS quadratic form, or a stronger RG topology proven to dominate those seminorms.
Plane-safe positivity must extend to observables whose support approaches t=0 without generating negative renormalized boundary terms.

falsifiers: Concrete falsifier: find f_i in A_+^{gi} and c_i such that all regulated q_{iota f,c}(S_{a,L}) are nonnegative, but the advertised RG convergence does not determine lim q_{iota f,c}; then the topology is too weak for OS positivity.

Concrete falsifier: construct two continuum extensions agreeing on ordinary gauge-invariant local Schwinger functions but giving different signs for one reflected Wilson-loop quadratic form; then the selected observables do not separate the same theory.
Concrete falsifier: a reflection-plane counterterm contributes a finite negative boundary term to q_{f,c}(S) after epsilon down to 0, invalidating the plane-safe extension step.
Concrete falsifier: gauge fixing introduces BRST or quotient degrees of freedom so that reflection positivity holds only before quotienting or only on a different algebra than A_+^{gi}.
Concrete falsifier: finite-volume reflection positivity uses a lattice reflection plane that has no compatible continuum reflection action under the chosen cutoff-removal maps.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 168 turns the branch from naming a topology into a falsifiable proof obligation. The closed-cone preservation theorem is valid and nearly formal in tau_OS, so it should not consume more discovery effort. The real Yang-Mills content is now the domination estimate: every reflected OS probe, including nonlocal gauge-invariant probes and reflection-plane limits, must be controlled by the actual RG convergence. This also shows why the same-theory condition is not cosmetic; changing the test algebra can make the positivity bridge true while no longer proving positivity for the intended Yang-Mills theory.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Define the smallest plane-safe gauge-invariant probe class A_{+,epsilon}^{gi}; check whether existing multiscale bounds control the doubled insertion (theta f)g uniformly as epsilon decreases. The decisive calculation is a Wilson-loop pair mirrored across t=0, because it stresses nonlocality, reflection covariance, and boundary contact behavior simultaneously.
